== Biography ==
Mary was born about 1807, calculated from her monument age at death. She is the daughter of [[Glasgow-3324|William Glasgow]] and [[Stewart-72380|Elizabeth Stewart]].


First Larne Presbyterian Church’s surviving history says Mary Glasgow was the church sexton in October 1829. She received accommodation valued at £2 rent, quarterly payments and an additional payment at each communion<ref>https://www.firstlarne.org.uk/sites/default/files/A%20Short%20History.pdf</ref>

Mary Glasgow, daughter of William and Elizabeth, may have been the Mary Glasgow employed as sexton of First Larne Presbyterian Church in 1829.

The surviving 1831 Larne census extract contains several female-headed Glasgow households, including:

Jane Glasgow: no males, five females;
Anne Glasgow: no males, two females;
Mary Glasgow: no males, four females.

The return gives numbers, not ages or relationships.

https://virtualtreasury.ie/item/VRTI-CEN-1831-3-29-9-3-LarneTown

Mary died on '''18 October 1844 aged 37''', according to the family monument, which calls her the daughter of William and Elizabeth.<ref>"Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim," ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', second series 6 (1900), [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up p. 47], William Glasgow family monument transcription; original printed page inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-3324]] is assessed at 98% (proved). The Larne monument transcription in Ulster Journal of Archaeology6(1900), p.47 identifies Mary in William and Elizabeth Glasgow’s family, alongside William’s 1816 death. The death entry 18 October 1844 aged 37 defines this child independently of speculative later matches.

Selected father-profile identity and paternal relationship; maternal identity is separate.

Next useful test: Compare the original stone and William’s 1815 will, PRONI D300/1/5/49.

Source basis already held: [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up "Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim," Ulster Journal of Archaeology, second series, vol. 6 (1900), p. 47, Glasgow inscriptions; page image (https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Possible identity with the 1843 bride ===
[[Glasgow-4181|Mary (Glasgow) McGavock]], the spinster of Larne named in a marriage settlement with John McGavock on 10 February 1843, is a possible identity for this Mary.<ref>Registry of Deeds, Ireland, McGavock–Glasgow settlement, 10 February 1843, registered 18 February; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-FQ3Q opening image 499] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-F3BZ continuation image 500], originals inspected 21 September 2026.</ref> The probable matching wife in John McGavock's 1851 Larne census return died in '''autumn 1843 aged 37''', whereas this family's monument records '''18 October 1844 aged 37'''.<ref>National Archives of Ireland, 1851 census, Larne, Cross Street, house 1, John McGavock household; [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/view-pdf/?doc=007246521_00320&c19=true household/marriages] and [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/view-pdf/?doc=007246521_00321&c19=true deceased-household table], original return.</ref> The bride's separate profile is provisional, not proof of two women. The settlement mentions payment by the executors of [[Glasgow-4180|Hugh Glasgow]] but does not state kinship. This Mary's monument-proved father [[Glasgow-3324|William]] is retained. If the two Marys prove identical, the new profile's uncertain Hugh-father hypothesis must be withdrawn. Resolve the conflicting death years through the original stone, marriage/burial registers and property title before merging.

The Larne death place is inferred from the family and monument context and is marked uncertain; the inscription does not explicitly give a place of death.
